title: Nihongi
attributionNote: Completed in 720 CE under imperial commission, with Prince Toneri among its chief editors and Ō no Yasumaro among the compilers. The work is a court compilation rather than the book of a single author, so no single author is recorded.
description: The Nihon Shoki, completed eight years after the Kojiki, is the first of the six national histories. In thirty books it covers the age of the gods and then the reigns from Jimmu to the abdication of Empress Suiko in 628, quoting variant traditions side by side and drawing on continental chronicles for its dating.
historicalContext: Written in classical Chinese at the court's command, the Nihongi was meant to stand beside the Kojiki as the official record of the realm's origins. Its reign-by-reign annalistic form, its variant readings ('in one writing it is said') and its use of Chinese chronological models make it both a religious and a historiographical document.
availabilityNote: Streamed from Wikisource book by book at read time. Aston's 1896 translation is public domain; the classical Chinese text is not included.
